_README: Error rates for the rules that decide what the Index publishes. Each was measured against a hand-judged sample drawn by seeded shuffle; `npm run validate -- --full` redraws the same samples. Intervals are Wilson 95%.

overExclusion.how: full census of every withdrawn domain; homepage fetched, title and description read by hand
overExclusion.note: This is the classifier's own rate, which is what it should be: all 4 are corrected in classification-overrides.json, so the shipped pipeline removes none of them today. Checking this turned up that 2 of the 4 — dragonball-super.com and strikerreport.com — had their verdict fixed but were never put back in the audit list, so their report pages were live while they stayed out of the ranking and out of every weekly run. Both are now in submitted.txt and rejoin at the next run.

asShipped.note: after overrides. The 4 raw errors are the measure of the model, not of what the site publishes.

found: az24.vn — a Vietnamese lottery-results site; now excluded in classification-overrides.json
underExclusion.how: `npm run probe-filter` and `SEED=1337 npm run probe-filter` — two draws of 66 from the sorted kept pool, 127 distinct domains (5 overlap). A domain is called unreadable only after three surfaces give nothing: homepage on the auditor's bot UA, the same request on a browser UA, then robots.txt and sitemap.xml at HTTP 200. Body text scanned for adult, gambling and piracy vocabulary; every hit hand-judged.

wholePopulationBound.how: the far edge: the one hand-verified error, plus all 16 domains that stayed unreadable, plus all 16 judged only from robots.txt and sitemap.xml — counted as wrong keeps. Those 16 rest on URL paths, which say what a site is made of but are not the page, so a bound that leans on them is not the far edge.
wholePopulationBound.says: at the far edge of the interval, at most 34.2% of kept domains are wrongly kept. Nothing weaker than this covers the whole sample.
wholePopulationBound.intermediate: Counting only the unresolved as wrong, and trusting the robots/sitemap tier: 17/127 = 13.4%, 95% CI 8.5-20.4%.

underExclusion.sensitivity: livescore.com is the closest call and was kept: its title and purpose are live football scores, and the rule judges primary purpose, but it runs a betting-affiliate directory. Counted as a wrong keep instead, the rate is 2/111 = 1.8%, 95% CI 0.5-6.3%.
underExclusion.reproducibility: The earlier 0/121 was measured against the leaderboard in score order, so the weekly run reshuffled the pool and the same seed drew an entirely different sample — reproducible in name only, and it failed silently. The pool is now sorted and fingerprinted, the fingerprint is printed on every run and published here, and POOL_HASH=<hash> makes a changed pool say so. Two consecutive runs of seed 2026 drew the identical 66 domains; one domain's live fetch differed (gamma.app readable in one, walled in the next), and the conservative run is what is published.
underExclusion.supersedes: 0/44 readable CI 0-8.0%; the single-seed 0/61; and 0/121 CI 0-3.1%, whose pool no longer exists. The honest reading is that the kept side was never 0 — the sample that would have found az24.vn had not been drawn yet.
underExclusion.tiers: 95 judged on the page itself, 16 on robots/sitemap only, 16 on nothing.
underExclusion.sampling: Pseudo-random with a fixed seed, not a convenience sample: the full kept pool is sorted to canonicalise it, then shuffled by the seed, so every member of the pool can be drawn and the draw is identical on any machine. Sorting fixes the order the shuffle acts on; it does not select.
underExclusion.handJudged: The one error, az24.vn, was judged by hand from the site's own title and navigation. livescore.com is a judgement call published as a sensitivity, not counted as an error: by the stated rule — primary purpose — a live-scores site that sells betting affiliate placement is kept.

inSample.how: seed 42, 15 sites x 4 categories — the set the rule was tuned against, so not evidence of accuracy

heldOut.how: seed 99, disjoint from seed 42, 10 readable sites x 4 categories
heldOut.note: SUPERSEDED as the current rate by heldOutPostFix. Retained because it is what the rule scored before clarin.com and grow.google were fixed.

heldOutPostFix.how: seed 777, disjoint from seeds 42 and 99; 14 readable sites x 4 categories, judged by hand
heldOutPostFix.note: measured after the clarin.com and grow.google fixes. Pre-fix on seed 99 the held-out rate was 10%.
heldOutPostFix.checked: mega.nz 0/20 and bankofamerica.com 5/20 looked like under-credits and were verified correct: mega.nz serves a one-word JS shell, bankofamerica.com links no privacy page from its homepage HTML.

falsePositive.note: three detections is too few to support a rate; each was hand-checked against platform runtime config, not the detector's own patterns

shopMembership.how: seed 11, 20 domains marked shop, judged by hand
shopMembership.boundary: A shop is a site whose primary purpose is selling goods or services to the public and where a visitor can start a purchase. News, reference, social, government, sport, banking and free tools are not shops even when they sell a subscription. Whether to narrow this to retail only is a product decision, not a measurement one.
